questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: What makes a pipeline a pipeline
questions.stem: A train dispatcher logs car movements into a scheduled ETL that lands a table; what makes it a pipeline?

options.text: It moves data through staged steps automatically
It stores data in a spreadsheet
It has a single manual query

questions.explanation: A pipeline moves data through automated staged steps. Storage, reports, or manual queries alone do not make a pipeline.

provenance.author: bank-team-data-science
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.stem: A dispatcher needs minute-level delay alerts; should the pipeline be batch or streaming?

options.text: Batch hourly because it is cheaper

questions.explanation: Minute-level alerts require streaming. Batch intervals are too coarse for timely detection.

provenance.author: bank-team-data-science

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: What a late record does to a window
questions.stem: Explain what a late-arriving record does to an already closed window.

answer.exemplar: A late record arrives after the window has closed, so it is either dropped or routed to a side output, and the window result is not recomputed unless late data handling is configured.

questions.explanation: Closed windows do not automatically include late data. Side outputs or allowed lateness handle it.

provenance.author: bank-team-data-science

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.stem: A dispatcher retries a write; what property prevents duplicate rows?
questions.explanation: Idempotent writes produce the same result when repeated, preventing duplicates. Speed or batch size do not ensure correctness.

provenance.author: bank-team-data-science

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.stem: Events arrive out of order; what does the watermark track?

options.text: The maximum event time seen so far

questions.explanation: The watermark tracks progress in event time, usually the max event time seen minus allowed lateness. Wall-clock time is processing time.

questions.topic: A schema change and the consumer it breaks

options.text: A consumer reading only unchanged columns
A consumer selecting the renamed column by name
A consumer using a view with no column reference

questions.explanation: Consumers referencing the renamed column by name break. Row counts or untouched columns survive.

questions.explanation: Row count can match while duplicates replace distinct rows. A missing table or empty set would change the count.

answer.exemplar: A backfill reprocesses historical data in bulk and can overwhelm or skew the live path, so a separate path with its own rate limits and checkpoints avoids disrupting current data.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: What a late record does to a window
questions.stem: Explain how to handle late records in a streaming window.

answer.exemplar: Configure allowed lateness and route very late records to a side output or dead-letter, then optionally recompute affected windows.

questions.explanation: Allowed lateness keeps windows open briefly; side outputs capture very late data. Recomputation handles corrections.

provenance.author: bank-team-data-science

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.stem: Explain how to make a pipeline write idempotent.

answer.exemplar: Use a deterministic key and upsert or insert-if-not-exists keyed on that id, so repeated deliveries overwrite rather than append rows.

questions.explanation: A deterministic key plus upsert makes repeats safe. Append-only writes create duplicates.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.stem: Max event time is 100 and allowed lateness is 5; what is the watermark?

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: A schema change and the consumer it breaks
questions.stem: Explain how to reduce consumer breakage when evolving a schema.

answer.exemplar: Add new columns as nullable or with defaults, avoid renaming or removing columns, and version the schema so consumers can migrate gradually.

questions.explanation: Additive nullable changes with versioning let consumers migrate. Renaming breaks references.

questions.explanation: Zero nulls checks not-null; distinct count equals row count checks uniqueness. Both are simple assertions.
